title: [News] AI, HBM Drive Memory Testing Demand: How China’s Suppliers Are Challenging an 80%-Import Market
key_facts: Imported equipment accounts for more than 80% of the installed base across China's back-end memory testing, per ijiwei.
Advantest holds over 50% of the global memory chip testing equipment market; Teradyne about 30% of the server memory segment.
ETNews: Digital Frontier and UniTest won a combined KRW 283.94 billion of HBM4 wafer tester orders from SK hynix this year.
China's TBSTest is expected to take nearly 15% of China's memory test-equipment market in 2026, per ijiwei.
Starting with HBM4, memory makers are increasingly using dedicated testing equipment.
quote_evidence: Imported equipment still accounts for more than 80% of China's installed base across back-end testing processes.
Advantest currently holds more than 50% of the global memory chip testing equipment market, the report notes.
TBSTest has secured orders for more than 300 systems from several leading memory customers in China and overseas, and is expected to capture nearly 15% of China's memory ATE market in 2026.
why_it_matters_hint: Testing demand grows as AI memory gets more complex, and Chinese makers are trying to replace imported machines.
notes: TrendForce relays ijiwei and ETNews; share figures are as reported by those outlets.
